requirements.statement: For each informative image that has a detailed description and uses aria-describedby, aria-describedby associates the detailed description.

routes.statement: The aria-describedby value lists the id of the area, or the ids of the passages, holding the detailed description, and assistive technologies render that content.

vérifier que le contenu de la description détaillée est correctement restitué par les technologies d’assistance

rationale.text: No link and candidate none. Whether the referenced content is the detailed description is judgment, and the methodology checks the result with assistive technologies, a prerequisite never met in v1, so a pass cannot be proven. One case looks mechanical: an aria-describedby whose ids match no element in the page associates nothing. It is not claimed, because the fault would rest on a witness that is not surely in scope: the test covers only images that carry information and that are accompanied by a detailed description, and both are judgment. A decorative image with a stray aria-describedby, or an image whose description is given by another means, may carry the same broken attribute. What would raise it: official text that puts every image using aria-describedby in scope, or a definition of an informative image that code can apply. No axe-core rule is tagged for this test. Applicability is judgment. Needs is assistive_tech, because the methodology asks for it.
